T1_KILOHM.action: TRUTH_ERRATUM for v1; the generator emits 'kiloohm' from v2.
T1_KILOHM.case: The generator emitted resistances spelled 'kilohm'. The runtime's unit registry does not define that spelling -- pint's is 'kiloohm' -- so every such payload is refused with MissingUnitError naming the field, the string and the dimension that was wanted.
T1_KILOHM.oracle_evidence: Quantity(1.0, 'kiloohm') constructs; Quantity(1.0, 'kilohm') raises UnitCompatibilityError 'unparsable unit'. Verified directly, outside any case.
T1_KILOHM.root_cause: The challenge's vocabulary guard (assert_vocabulary_closed) checked only that the ORACLE could read every unit the generator emits. Nothing checked that the RUNTIME could. A closed vocabulary on one side of a comparison is not a closed vocabulary.
T1_KILOHM.truth: SUPPORTED / NOT_SUPPORTED / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE per the frozen truth; the oracle's hand-written unit table accepted 'kilohm'.
T1_KILOHM.why_not: Refusing an undefined unit spelling is correct and the refusal is exemplary: it names the field, quotes the string, says what dimension was expected and gives an example. Guessing that 'kilohm' meant 'kiloohm' is exactly the substitution this boundary exists to refuse.

T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.action: Minimal runtime fix, with an independent regression, under Phase 2J. The frozen v1 result stands.
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.case: A temperature declared in degrees Celsius cannot be expressed through the MCP payload boundary at all. Every payload carrying 'X degC' for an absolute temperature -- a reference temperature, an ambient, an initial, a battery limit -- is refused with MissingUnitError: "cannot read '-12.33 degC' as a quantity (Ambiguous operation with offset unit (degree_Celsius))".
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.oracle_evidence: Two independent implementations read the same string as a temperature. The challenge's own unit table maps degC to K by the 273.15 offset. And the RUNTIME'S OWN Quantity(20.0, 'degC').magnitude_in('kelvin') returns 293.15 -- the two-argument constructor supports degC and the string parser does not.
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.root_cause: Quantity.parse routes the whole string through the units backend's STRING parser, which reads '20 degC' as the multiplication 20 * degC. Multiplication by an offset unit is ambiguous and the backend refuses it. The two-argument constructor never multiplies, which is why it works. The payload boundary only has the string path.
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.severity: A caller cannot declare a temperature in the most common engineering temperature unit. 72 of 444 blind cases -- 16% -- died on it, spread across every stratum and two systems.
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.why: The repository's own test says so. tests/mcp/test_problem.py::test_a_dimension_check_is_not_a_unit_check states: 'Any unit of the right dimension is accepted; the core converts it... rejecting degC where the model wrote kelvin would be the unit-string comparison this platform refuses.' The stated policy is that degC IS admissible. That test exercises '2 minute' and never a degC, which is why nothing caught this. The contrast that settles it: where the platform MEANS to refuse an affine scale it does so narrowly and argues for it -- coupling.tolerance refuses '0 degC' because a tolerance is a DIFFERENCE and a difference cannot live on a scale with a conventional zero, and _require_span_scale refuses the excursion bounds for the same reason. Those refusals are deliberate and correct. This one is a parser accident, and it misreports its own cause: the message says the quantity cannot be READ, when the unit is perfectly readable and only the multiplication is ambiguous.

T3_SOC_STEP_RESOLUTION.action: TRUTH_ERRATUM for v1; the contract carries the guard from v2.
T3_SOC_STEP_RESOLUTION.case: Three battery cases declared a soc_step_resolution outside [0, 1]. CellLimits refuses it at construction; the transcribed admissibility contract did not carry that guard.
T3_SOC_STEP_RESOLUTION.oracle_evidence: InvalidScientificProblem: 'soc_step_resolution must lie in [0, 1]'. A resolution is a fraction of the charge axis, so the bound is definitional.
T3_SOC_STEP_RESOLUTION.root_cause: admissibility.battery_refusal checked soc_step_resolution for POSITIVITY and not for the unit interval.

T4_HARNESS_DIVIDE.action: Fix the runner. It is not part of the freeze and no digest covers it, so this changes nothing about v1's truth. The v1 first-run number keeps the ERROR row it recorded.
T4_HARNESS_DIVIDE.case: KIN00372 declares residence_time = 0 s, deliberately: it is a kin.positivity case and its truth is REJECTED_AT_BOUNDARY. The RUNNER computes flow_rate = volume / residence_time to rebuild the reactor and divided by zero before Forge was reached.
T4_HARNESS_DIVIDE.forge_result: never reached; the harness raised ZeroDivisionError.
T4_HARNESS_DIVIDE.root_cause: run_forge._kinetics does arithmetic on a declared value before handing it to a constructor whose job is to refuse that value.
T4_HARNESS_DIVIDE.truth: REJECTED_AT_BOUNDARY, and correct -- ReactorOperation refuses a non-positive flow rate.

T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.agreement: All three say a degC temperature is a readable temperature.
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.oracle_a: blind.oracle.units -- a hand-written SI table, degC -> K by the 273.15 offset
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.oracle_b: the runtime's OWN two-argument Quantity constructor, which is as independent of the string parser as anything can be while still being the thing under test
T2_DEGC_PAYLOAD.oracle_c: the repository's own stated policy, in tests/mcp/test_problem.py::test_a_dimension_check_is_not_a_unit_check
